chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal from Uqbah ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): In

a man who bought goods from a man and finalized the deal, except that he left the goods with him and did not take possession of them. He said, 'I will come to you tomorrow, if God wills,' and the goods were stolen. Whose money would they be? He said, 'From the money of the owner of the goods who is in his house, until he takes possession of the goods and takes them out of his house. And when he takes them out of his house, the buyer is liable for their value until he returns their money to him.'

key_terms.أَوْجَبَهُ: finalized the deal / made it binding

ai.seo_question: Who bears the risk of loss for goods left with the seller after a sale is finalized?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that liability (daman) in a sale is contingent upon actual physical removal (kharuj) from the seller's domain, not merely the verbal agreement or payment. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that risk transfers with possession rather than contract, ensuring fairness when goods remain in the seller's custody. It highlights the practical distinction between ownership rights and liability for loss in commercial transactions.
